controls.name: Marfa lights viewing area
controls.record: Reported since Ellison's 1883 account; continuous modern reporting; instrumented study by Texas State / SHSU physics groups 2004-2008.
controls.conventional: Bunnell's programme attributed the MAJORITY of observed events to vehicle headlights on US-67, with a documented unexplained residual. Grade B, not A, for exactly that reason.
controls.coord_basis: Official TxDOT viewing area on US-90 east of Marfa. Source region is Mitchell Flat, 5-15 km SW -- see section 5, coordinate error.

controls.name: Toppenish Ridge / Yakama Reservation
controls.gazetteer: Toppenish Ridge, Yakima County, Washington, USA
controls.record: W.J. Vogel, fire control officer for the Yakama Nation, logged recurrent luminous phenomena 1972-1974 in an agency capacity; the log was written up independently and is the single institutional primary record here.
controls.conventional: None established for the logged events.
controls.coord_basis: Toppenish Ridge, the ridge line named in the reports.

controls.name: Silver Cliff cemetery
controls.gazetteer: Silver Cliff, Custer County, Colorado, USA
controls.record: Lay reports from the 1880s mining era onward; National Geographic feature, 1969.
controls.conventional: Reflection of town and starlight off headstones is plausible and has never been established or excluded.
controls.coord_basis: The cemetery itself, which is the named locale.

controls.name: San Luis Valley (Crestone-Hooper corridor)
controls.record: Sustained regional compilation by C. O'Brien, 1990s, plus lay reports.
controls.conventional: Not established. The record is regional rather than point-located, which is itself a weakness for a 2 km-radius leg.
controls.coord_basis: Valley floor midpoint of the corridor the compilation names.

controls.name: Uinta Basin / Skinwalker Ranch
controls.gazetteer: Fort Duchesne, Uintah County, Utah, USA
controls.record: Frank Salisbury's 1974 Uinta Basin compilation is the older and cleaner record; the ranch-specific material is later.
controls.coord_basis: The ranch parcel named in the later material. GRADE D: the modern record is entangled with a commercial interest, which is what the grade rule penalises, and the site is kept only because the rule is applied rather than the site chosen.

controls.name: Trout Lake / Mount Adams
controls.gazetteer: Trout Lake, Klickitat County, Washington, USA
controls.record: Recurrent reports from a single primary observer's property, 1990s on.
controls.coord_basis: Trout Lake valley, the named locale.
